newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria court to rule on FPB insolvency by end-96.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria court to rule on FPB insolvency by end-96.

text.p: The Sofia City Court is expected to rule on an insolvency suit against Bulgaria's First Private Bank filed by the central bank within 14 days, court officials said on Wednesday.
"The court will announce its decision within 14 days," a court official told reporters.

The central bank placed the FPB in receivership on May 17 dismissing its management and appointing sequestrators to establish its financial state. Two weeks later the central bank opened bankruptcy procedures against Bulgaria's biggest private bank.
After a seven-hour session on Wednesday the court turned down FPB's demand for new financial expertise which would adjust the bank's assets to current market prices.
It was expected to include immaterial assets like software and staff qulification.
The FPB owes some 31 billion levs to the State Savings Bank and the central bank which were lent to it as refinancing.
The bank owes a further 20 billion levs paid out by Post Bank as compensation for individual and company deposits.

The BNB has placed 14 or one quarter of Bulgaria's banks in receivership and has so far filed insolvency suits against nine local commercial banks in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to close debt-ridden banks in a bid to stabilise the shaky banking sector.
On Tuesday the court postponed ruling on Mineralbank until March.
